definition: Techniques for embedding a detectable signal into AI-generated content (text, images, audio) to allow later identification of its AI origin.
details: Watermarking is explored as one approach to help distinguish AI-generated content from human-created content, supporting transparency and combating misuse like disinformation, though robustness against removal remains a technical challenge.

explainer.lead: Watermarking embeds a detectable signal in AI-generated text, images, or audio so its AI origin can later be identified. It matters as a transparency measure against misuse such as disinformation, but robustness against removal remains a technical challenge.

tiers.eli5: Like a hidden signature woven into a picture that shows it was made by a machine, so people can check later where it came from.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers embed a statistical or perceptual signal during generation that a detector can later test for. The main pitfall is that determined editing or regeneration can strip the mark, so robustness is the hard part.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, generation is modified so that outputs carry a signal detectable by a corresponding detector while remaining imperceptible to users. Known limit: signals are not reliably robust against removal.

explainer.example: A text generator subtly biases word choices so a detector can flag the passage as machine-written; paraphrasing the text may erase that bias.
